direction.question: Can one autonomous scientific system transfer across instruments and scientific domains while keeping experiments safe, uncertainty calibrated, provenance complete, and results independently reproducible?
direction.closureCriteria: Pre-register transfer from at least one training domain or instrument to two materially different targets; require calibrated abstention and human safety gates; preserve machine-readable lineage from hypothesis through raw data and analysis; compare against domain-specific automation and human teams; and have an independent lab reproduce a claimed result from the released record.
partialResults: A 2026 autonomous laboratory agent operates scanning probe microscopy through a domain-specific model and deterministic modular interface. AI Scientist-v2 automates computational machine-learning research across several subdomains, and earlier Coscientist work demonstrated bounded chemistry workflows. These systems establish real partial autonomy, but none closes cross-instrument, cross-domain transfer with independent physical reproduction and calibrated uncertainty.
starters: Individual: Build a provenance-first agent for DiscoveryBench and ScienceAgentBench that must produce an executable rerun bundle, calibrated confidence, and an explicit abstention whenever evidence or permissions are missing.

Small lab: Connect the same policy layer to two instruments, or one instrument plus a high-fidelity simulator, preregister transfer tasks, retain human safety approval, and have a second operator independently repeat the result.

Well-funded lab: Run a two-domain, two-site autonomous-science challenge with different instruments, robotic sample handling, blind replication, machine-readable lineage, uncertainty calibration, and independent safety and research-integrity oversight.

noveltyReview.scope: Targeted arXiv searches for autonomous laboratories, self-driving labs, AI scientists, laboratory agents, cross-domain scientific agents, instrument control, reproducibility, provenance, Coscientist, AI Scientist v2, and 2025-2026 systems and benchmarks; reference chaining from representative systems and benchmark papers.
noveltyReview.note: High confidence that transferable cross-instrument, cross-domain autonomy with independent physical replication remains open. Domain-specific and computational systems are already substantial, so the gap must not be described as absence of autonomous science. No priority claim is made.

counterexamples: Autonomous Laboratory Agent controls real-time atomic-resolution scanning probe microscopy using a customized domain model, deterministic validation, and modular orchestration; it remains a single instrument family and domain.

AI Scientist-v2 performs template-free computational ML research and produced workshop-level manuscripts, including one accepted at a workshop with a high acceptance rate; it does not demonstrate transfer across physical instruments or independent experimental reproduction.

Coscientist and other self-driving-lab systems demonstrate chemistry and materials workflows, while DiscoveryBench and ScienceAgentBench show that broad data-science agents still solve only a minority of realistic tasks.

benchmarks: A preregistered cross-instrument protocol with an independent physical reproduction endpoint
datasets: Open Reaction Database and Materials Project for cross-domain data work, plus raw instrument traces and complete experiment lineage

estimated.individual: One to four GPUs and data-only or simulated laboratories; no unsupervised wet-lab or physical actuation.
estimated.smallLab: Four to sixteen GPUs, two API-controlled instruments or one instrument plus simulator, technician time, metrology, and safety review.
estimated.wellFundedLab: Thirty-two or more GPUs, two domains and multiple workcells, robotic sample handling, instrument engineers, metrology, research-integrity controls, and an independent replication site.

direction.crowdedness: High for computational science agents, medium for domain-specific self-driving labs, and low for the same system transferring across physical domains and sites.
direction.tractability: High for data-only provenance studies, medium for a single-instrument system, and low for cross-domain transfer with independent physical reproduction.
